methods.label: LoRA L3 (unit-label FT)

l4d_batch_detail.method: per unit: unit_forward_s x n_questions_kept / unit_n_questions, summed, / 2,656

notes: one model = the largest of the three folds (fold0, 2 GPUs DDP): GPU-h = (finished_utc - started_utc) x world_size from l4d_ft/build/status/fold<k>.json; includes model load and 4 dev evals per fold. Pure train_s x 2 would be lower (train_s field).
A real deployment model trained on all three folds' data would see ~1.5x the questions; not measured.
Not counted: smoke/speed tests, dev re-selection runs, the layer1/placebo/original eval predictions, the old-LoRA (decision_ft) training, engineering time.

labelling = sum of per-unit `seconds` in l4d/build/gold_layer1.jsonl (dynamic gold: compile + traced runs + fault injection, dell i5-12500 CPU, 8 threads; per-unit wall time inside a worker thread, so ~CPU-thread time). Priced at the GPU rental rate as a deliberate upper bound. layer3 gold is eval-only and not part of the deployment cost.

break_even_basis: ours = one_off.usd_one_off_total_used_for_break_even + N x lora_l4d_opt batch rental per unit; cloud = N x billed per unit; N = ceil(one_off / (cloud - ours)); 'never' when ours per unit >= cloud per unit
notes: Cloud = what we were billed, with DeepSeek prefix caching and off-peak scheduling (peak gate in llm/llmlane/pricing.py); Jev bills input tokens only (output free).
Local = GPU time only; excludes engineering time, the host machine, storage, idle GPU time between requests, and hardware purchase (rental rate already includes it implicitly).

Local batch for L4-D (opt.) is an estimate: the stored eval predictions asked the FULL question set; each unit's forward time is scaled by its kept/full question ratio (42 % kept). The latency300 pruned-vs-full forward ratio is given as a cross-check in l4d_batch_detail.lat300_check.
Local units are processed one unit per forward batch (as in eval and latency300). Batching several units per forward would lower GPU-s per unit; not measured.
Old LoRA L1/L3 rows are secondary (much lower macro-F1).
macro_f1 from deadfree_quality.json; latency_s = c1 e2e median from latency_deadfree.csv (primary rows).
